This bill is part of a package that would create Renew Australia, a new body to oversee the shift to clean energy.
The authority would be tasked with planning and managing the change in Australia's electricity system.
The bill would start on the day a budget appropriation funds the authority.
Sets the authority's role to plan and drive the energy transition.
Delays commencement until budget funding is provided.
The authority itself and communities affected by the closure of coal-fired power stations.

The Renew Australia Bill 2016 was introduced to create a $500 million authority to drive a transition to at least 90% renewable electricity by 2030, with a $250 million clean energy transition fund for coal workers and communities, pollution intensity standards for staged closure of coal-fired power stations starting with Hazelwood, and a target to double energy productivity while increasing electricity generation by 50%.
